text: The accounting entry set, the chart-of-accounts reference and the posting type a match value maps to stay with the ledger and with Finance, and this service posts the facts of the matched receipt — case, proceeds, receipt, amount, value date, match value and route — as one item on the ledger interface; the mapping is held as data of the interface configuration and no account, cost centre or amount rule is written in code.
why: No read source publishes the entry set of a route or the posting type of a match value, and the ledger books the entries by its own accounting rules.
read: FSD P8 A2.7; TSD P8 T3.1; R-SET-14, R-SET-18, R-DIS-54; ITG story section 19
applied_in: RWB-P8-E4047-APP s2, s3, s4, s8 (BR5), s13
confirm: Business analyst, P8, with Finance and the ledger owner
impact: One data-held mapping and one posting facts block; no accounting value is compiled, and a chart change needs no release.

text: The posting step runs when the receipt is matched, in the same run as the match, and the confirmation runs on the batch completion record of the source; the service sets no posting window, no Schedule and no Quartz row, and the monthly GL file is ACE's ingestion and not a timer of this service.
why: The FSD leaves the trigger open between a batch, an event and a timer, and the TSD gives the GL interface as a monthly file and the ALS booking as confirmed on the next day's load.
impact: No Schedule, no job table and no window; the posting is as current as the batch of its source.

text: The posting reference of a receipt is the payment code of the ACE payment record for its source, read through rwb-source-data on the batch date, and it is written to `proceeds.posting_ref` (DF-FIN-009); until the read is published the field carries the placeholder and the mapping is confirmed with the solution architect.
why: DF-FIN-009 says the core bank is its source and the data dictionary maps it to the ACE payment record with the instruction to confirm, and this service holds no ACE grant.
read: TSD P8 T3.1 DF-FIN-009; LDM v8 mapping row DF-FIN-009; DP-05
confirm: Solution architect, with the P1 contract owner
impact: One optional column and one consumed read; an ALS and a GL reference that differ need a second column and are not assumed here.

text: No posting-result event is published in this run: the confirmed reference on the proceeds row and `GET /proceeds` are how the fact is announced, and a posting event is raised with the event catalogue only if a consumer needs it.
why: The catalogue holds 26 published events and none reports a posting or its reference, and this story owns no event of the three the service holds.
read: Event and Messaging Design v4 Events sheet; context pack P8 events
impact: No outbox row and no schema of this story; a consumer reads the fact on the operation until an event exists.

text: The ledger and ALS interface identifier, transport, layout, result codes, retry intervals and exception message are rows of rwb-integration's interface configuration read at run time, and this story builds against the `deliverFile` activity contract and its fake from Day 1; MSG-P2-001 keeps its identifier and its wording stays with that service.
why: No read source publishes those values and the outbound path is rwb-integration's by the ownership map and by REQ-DRI-006 and REQ-DRI-007.
read: TSD P8 T5.1; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 JOB-09; RWB-P2-E1007-CON
confirm: Solution architect, with the P2 interface owner
impact: No interface value and no file layout in this service; a new transport or retry value is a data change.

text: This story declares the two operations the ownership rows of P8 and TSD P8 T-A.1 hold, and the payments read that RWB-ITG-E4047-ITG section 12.2 assigns to rwb-payment is held as a documentation conflict until the ownership map and the API specification are corrected or the harness is changed.
why: One service can declare its operations once, and two sources disagree on whether a payments read exists.
read: Context pack P8; TSD P8 T-A.1; ITG story section 12.2
confirm: Solution architect, with the harness owner
impact: No operation is invented; the harness either reads the receipts through GET /proceeds or waits for the owner to publish the read.

text: A posting the ledger rejects stays an exception item on the interface row, with its retry, its task and its resend, and the receipt keeps no posting reference; any case state such as POSTING_REJECTED is the route service's on its own rule and is not raised here.
why: The rejection rules exist only for the debt-sale and write-off routes and no rule states a case move for a settlement or a sale receipt.
read: Routing logic v4 R-DS-32, R-DS-33, R-WO-22, R-WO-23; FSD P8 A2.7
confirm: Business analyst, P8, with the route owners
impact: The rejection path of this service ends at the item; no case state is written and no new rule is invented.

text: The two reads this story consumes — the posting reference and batch status of rwb-source-data and the rule in force of rwb-decision — are class C dependencies in fact, are built against those owners' published documents and fakes from Day 1, and are carried in sections 12.2 and 13 rather than in the metadata row the plan fixes at None.
why: The plan's C row is empty while the step needs both answers to satisfy the legacy criteria.
